Where the Parent's Log-Density Has a Kink

Source: R/distrib_penalty.R
distrib_kinks.Rd

Returns the points at which a separable penalty built on this distribution is not differentiable, derived from the distribution itself, or numeric(0) when there are none. Among the families that distributions7 ships, only the two Laplace parametrizations and the elastic net have a location in which the log-density is not smooth, so only these, with the location held by distributions7::fixed(), give a kink.

Usage

distrib_kinks(d)

Arguments

d

A univariate distributions7 object. An object without parent_distrib, or whose chain of parents has no level carrying fixed_params, gets numeric(0) without further inspection.

Value

A numeric vector of the confirmed kink points, possibly empty, with duplicates removed.

How a candidate is found

A distribution records in params_smooth the parameters in which its log-likelihood is differentiable, and for a location family a location that is not smooth is a kink in the argument at that location. A penalty is the negative log-density read at the coefficient, so a distributions7::fixed() wrapper that holds such a parameter at a value puts the kink at that value: fixed(laplace_distrib(), mu = 0) is a Laplace prior at zero and has a kink at zero, while fixed(laplace_distrib(), mu = 2) has one at two.

A free parameter gives no candidate, because its value is set by the hyperparameters at the time of each evaluation. A Laplace with a free location therefore has no reported kink.

The wrapper is recognized by the properties that it carries, parent_distrib and fixed_params, and not by its class, because the classes of the distributions7::fixed() wrapper are not exported and a family written outside distributions7 may hold its parameters in the same way. The chain of parent_distrib is walked from the outermost object down, and every level that carries fixed_params contributes candidates, so that truncated(fixed(laplace2_distrib(), mu = 0), lower = -1, upper = 3) has its kink at zero.

How a candidate is confirmed

A candidate is dropped when it is not finite or when it does not lie strictly inside the support of the outermost object, a point at the edge of the support not being a kink of the density on its support: a folded() Laplace held at zero has no kink at zero. Each remaining candidate is then tested by comparing the one-sided derivatives of the log-density across it at a probe point (probe_theta(), has_jump()), and a candidate at which the derivative does not jump is dropped. The inference from params_smooth supplies the points to test, and the test removes the candidates at which the density is smooth, for example a candidate that comes from a non-smooth parameter that is not a location. The test is made on the outermost object, so a wrapper that moves the point drops the candidate.

See also

distrib_penalty(), which calls this function when its argument kinks is NULL, penalty_kinks() for the kinks of a built penalty, has_jump() for the test.

Examples

# A Laplace held at a location: a kink at that location.
distrib_kinks(distributions7::fixed(distributions7::laplace_distrib(),
                                    mu = 0))
#> [1] 0
distrib_kinks(distributions7::fixed(distributions7::laplace_distrib(),
                                    mu = 2))
#> [1] 2

# A Gaussian is smooth everywhere, so there is no candidate.
distrib_kinks(distributions7::fixed(distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(),
                                    mu = 0))
#> numeric(0)

# A free location gives no candidate.
distrib_kinks(distributions7::laplace_distrib())
#> numeric(0)

# A fixed() level under another wrapper is found; the origin of a folded
# Laplace is the edge of its support and is dropped.
lap0 <- distributions7::fixed(distributions7::laplace2_distrib(), mu = 0)
distrib_kinks(distributions7::truncated(lap0, lower = -1, upper = 3))
#> [1] 0
distrib_kinks(distributions7::folded(lap0))
#> numeric(0)
